cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Handwriting – writing with a pen or pencil in the hand.

p.em: Example: Many people believe that beautiful handwriting is a lost art.

cosy-blockquote.p: Typing – the action or skill of writing something on a typewriter or computer keyboard.

p.em: Example: Fast typing is an essential skill for most modern office jobs.

cosy-blockquote.p: Keyboard – a panel of keys that operates a computer or typewriter.

p.em: Example: He prefers a mechanical keyboard because of the tactile feedback.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive – relating to the mental processes of perception, memory, and judgment.

p.em: Example: Writing by hand stimulates different cognitive networks than typing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Retention – the continued possession, use, or control of something (e.g. memory).

p.em: Example: Taking handwritten notes leads to much better information retention.

cosy-blockquote.p: Neurological – relating to the anatomy, functions, and organic disorders of nerves and the brain.

p.em: Example: Handwriting triggers a unique neurological response that typing cannot emulate.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tactile – relating to the sense of touch.

p.em: Example: The tactile sensation of pen on paper is very comforting.

cosy-blockquote.p: Digital – involving or relating to the use of computer technology.

p.em: Example: Our workplace has shifted completely from paper folders to digital files.

cosy-blockquote.p: Device – a thing made or adapted for a particular purpose, especially an electronic machine.

p.em: Example: A tablet is a highly versatile digital device for students.

cosy-blockquote.p: Productivity – the state or quality of being productive; output per unit of input.

p.em: Example: Typing allows you to write large amounts of text, boosting your office productivity.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
A: Elegant handwriting is a highly valued personal skill that shows discipline and character. B: Rapid typing allows professionals to record thoughts at the speed of speech.
★ Complete this sentence using inversion: 'Seldom do I write by hand, except when...'

A: Professional typing skills are essential for high-paying modern career paths. B: Writing by hand forces you to slow down and synthesize information.
★ Have you ever taken a speed test to measure your typing words per minute?

A: An ergonomic, mechanical keyboard provides satisfying feedback and speed. B: Pens offer unlimited freedom of movement, drawing, and custom layout.
★ Do you care about the design and tactile feel of your keyboard?

A: Studies show that handwriting stimulates key cognitive networks in the brain. B: Digital word processors free up your cognitive energy to focus on content.
★ Do you agree that typing requires less cognitive effort than writing by hand?

A: Taking notes by hand leads to significantly better memory retention of the material. B: Digital documents are easily searchable, so you do not need perfect mental retention.
★ Do you remember information better when you write it down on paper, improving retention?

A: Handwriting practice builds complex neurological connections between brain hemispheres. B: Online sharing offers instant global connection and collaboration.
★ Is a strong neurological stimulation your main goal when taking notes?

A: The tactile sensation of a physical pen gliding on paper is deeply satisfying. B: Smooth glass screens are much cleaner and do not require physical paper.
★ Do you enjoy the tactile feedback of physical keys or the silence of a touch screen?

A: Moving to a digital workspace allows for instant cloud backups and easy organization. B: Traditional paper folders protect you from screen fatigue and distraction.
★ Is your daily life almost 100% digital, or do you still use physical diaries?

A: A modern tablet device allows you to combine handwriting and digital sharing. B: A simple pen and paper require no charging and never crash.
★ What is your most essential electronic device for daily productivity?

A: Typing large amounts of text offers unparalleled speed and productivity. B: Handwriting forces a selective, slow process that is more intellectually productive.
★ Do you prioritize absolute speed and productivity when choosing how to take notes?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
A: Illegible handwriting can ruin a student's grades and cause professional confusion. B: Typing can make all documents look standardized and devoid of personality.
★ Have you ever failed to read your own handwriting after a long lecture?

A: Repetitive typing for hours can lead to physical issues like carpal tunnel syndrome. B: Writing by hand is slow and can cause hand cramps very quickly.
★ Does continuous typing make your hands or wrists feel stiff?

A: A loud keyboard in a shared office can be extremely irritating to colleagues. B: A physical pen limits your editing speed compared to a full QWERTY keyboard.
★ Do you get annoyed when colleagues type loudly on a mechanical keyboard?

A: Typing during lectures can lead to shallow cognitive processing of the information. B: Rigid handwriting methods can slow down students with motor skill issues, causing a cognitive block.
★ Have you ever felt that typing is too passive to stimulate your cognitive thinking?

A: Copying slides word-for-word on a laptop results in poor information retention. B: Paper notes can be easily lost, completely destroying any external retention of work.
★ How do you backup your notes to prevent the loss of critical information retention?

A: Excessive digital connectivity often leads to constant notification distractions, lowering neurological focus. B: A total lack of digital connectivity on paper prevents fast collaboration with peers.
★ Do you turn off your phone notifications when you need to focus deeply?

A: The flat, cold lack of any tactile feedback on touchscreens can feel unnatural. B: Physical paper lacks the convenient, fast editing options of digital systems.
★ Do you miss the tactile feel of real buttons when typing on a phone?

A: A purely digital life increases screen exposure, causing eye strain and poor sleep. B: Refusing to use digital tools makes you highly inefficient in the modern workplace.
★ Do you actively try to reduce your digital screen time on weekends?

A: A single broken device can lock you out of all your files and schedule. B: A pen and notebook can easily get physically damaged, wet, or lost.
★ Have you ever experienced a major panic when an electronic device stopped working?

A: Excessive focus on speed can lead to shallow, rushed writing, which is detrimental to productivty. B: A total disregard for speed and productivity makes you struggle to meet modern corporate deadlines.
★ Do you think our society is overly obsessed with speed and productivity?

ul.li: Incorrect: I write more fast with laptop → Correct: I write faster with a laptop ((Comparative form of 'fast' is 'faster'))
Incorrect: The handwriting is an art → Correct: Handwriting is an art ((No definite article for general activities))
Incorrect: It is depend of my mood → Correct: It depends on my mood ((Depends + on preposition))
